input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view in the Dashboard

## Description

Delivers a comparison view in the Dashboard where users select two or more
training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side,
plus a diff mode that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between
two selected runs. Today parameters and metrics are only visible on per-run
pages, so data scientists compare runs in exported spreadsheets; this epic
brings that comparison in-platform to support model promotion decisions.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the runs list in the Dashboard
- Side-by-side rendering of parameters and metrics for the selected runs
- Diff view for two selected runs highlighting which parameters and metrics
  changed between them
- The comparison works for both training runs and Data Science Pipelines
  runs, with no changes to the pipelines component itself (it continues to
  work as-is; run data is already surfaced per-run)
- Out of scope: automatic best-run selection or promotion; comparison across
  clusters or across projects

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user viewing the runs list, when they select two or more runs and
  open the comparison, then the parameters and metrics of all selected runs
  are displayed side by side.
- Given two runs selected in the comparison view, when the user opens the
  diff view, then the parameters and metrics that changed between the two
  runs are highlighted.
- Given runs produced by Data Science Pipelines, when included in a
  comparison, then their parameters and metrics render correctly with no
  change to the pipelines component (passive-component validation).
- Comparisons remain within a single project; cross-project and cross-cluster
  comparison are rejected or unavailable.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters
  and metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1): run "diff" view highlighting which parameters and metrics
  changed between two selected runs — bundled with HLR-1 because it shares
  the same comparison UI surface and data; splitting would duplicate that
  surface.

# Run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Registered model versions record a link back to the run (training or
pipeline) that produced them, and that lineage is exposed through the Model
Registry so any consumer — including the Dashboard's registry UI — can
resolve which run created a given model version. This is the metadata
foundation that lets a comparison be opened from the Model Registry.

## Scope

- Association of a registered model version with the run that produced it,
  recorded when the version is registered
- The run reference is stored as model version metadata and retrievable
  through the registry's API
- No change to run execution, pipeline behavior, or the registration
  workflow's existing fields beyond the new lineage reference

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, when the version is retrieved
  from the registry, then it carries a reference to the producing run.
- The lineage reference is readable through the registry's existing API
  surface without custom tooling.
- Given model versions registered before this change, when queried, then they
  continue to function (no migration breakage; absence of lineage on legacy
  versions is handled gracefully).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them (metadata portion of the requirement).

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

From a registered model version in the Dashboard's Model Registry section,
users can open a run comparison involving the run that produced that version.
This makes promotion decisions actionable directly from the registry without
navigating back to the runs list to find the candidate runs.

## Scope

- Entry point in the registry UI on a registered model version that opens the
  run comparison view with the version's producing run included
- Graceful handling for model versions that carry no recorded run lineage
- Requires the run comparison view capability in the Dashboard and run
  lineage recorded on registered model versions (both delivered by other work
  in this strategy)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a recorded producing run, when the
  user invokes the comparison entry point in the registry UI, then a
  comparison including that run is displayed in the comparison view.
- Given a registered model version without a recorded producing run, when
  viewed in the registry UI, then the comparison entry point is absent or
  disabled without error.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): "a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" (UI
  portion of the requirement).

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

Product documentation covering the run comparison workflow end to end:
selecting and comparing runs from the runs list, reading the diff view, and
opening a comparison from the Model Registry. Gives data scientists a single
reference for the in-platform comparison workflow that replaces exported
spreadsheets.

## Scope

- New or updated documentation topics covering the comparison workflow from
  the runs list (multi-select, side-by-side view, diff view)
- Documentation covering opening a comparison from a registered model version
  in the Model Registry
- Screenshots and procedure steps reflecting the implemented behavior

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers starting a comparison from the runs list: selecting
  two or more runs, viewing parameters and metrics side by side, and reading
  the diff view.
- Documentation covers opening a comparison from a registered model version
  in the Model Registry.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  before publication (accuracy validation against the shipped comparison
  view, registry lineage, and registry entry point).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry.

# Decomposition: RHAISTRAT-9015 — Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs

Strategy status: Refinement Done. Strategy priority: Major. All three affected
components (Dashboard, Model Registry, Data Science Pipelines) are present in
architecture context (rhoai-3.0, all GA, all Konflux onboarded) — no onboarding
chains required.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E001 | Run comparison view in the Dashboard | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E002 | Run lineage on registered model versions | Implementation | Model Registry | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E003 | Open run comparison from the Model Registry | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E004 | Document the run comparison workflow | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P1 |

Notes on the epic set:

- **No Investigation epics.** The strategy lists "Open Questions: None" and
  contains no conditional ADRs, pending reviews, or external dependencies.
  Remaining unknowns (e.g., how run parameters/metrics are bulk-fetched, how
  the run link is stored on a model version) are implementation details the
  owning teams resolve — they do not change which epics exist.
- **Data Science Pipelines is passive.** It is listed as affected, but no HLR
  requires a change to it: the Dashboard already surfaces per-run parameters
  and metrics for pipeline runs. Validation that comparisons work against
  pipeline runs is an acceptance criterion on E001. No separate validation
  epic: the Dashboard team performs that validation as part of E001.
- **HLR-3 (P1) is bundled into E001 (P0).** The diff view shares the same
  comparison UI surface and data as the side-by-side view; it is not
  independently deferrable (Step 4: tightly coupled to the same
  implementation surface — splitting would build the same UI surface twice).
- **HLR-2 spans two components** and is split accordingly: the lineage
  metadata belongs to Model Registry (E002), the UI entry point belongs to
  Dashboard (E003). Splitting also avoids making the P0 epic depend on P1
  lineage work.
- **E004 priority is P1**, not P2: per the docs-authoring priority exception,
  priority derives from the strategy frontmatter (Major → P1).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Run comparison view (Dashboard, P0)"] --> E003["E003 Open comparison from registry (Dashboard, P1)"]
    E002["E002 Run lineage on model versions (Model Registry, P1)"] --> E003
    E001 --> E004["E004 Documentation (P1)"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

Roots: E001 and E002 run in parallel. Critical path length: 3
(E001 → E003 → E004, equivalently E002 → E003 → E004).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | 13 (framework/surface → consumer) | The registry entry point's code builds against the comparison view surface delivered by the Dashboard comparison work; it cannot be built independently of that UI surface. |
| E002 → E003 | 13 (artifact → consumer) | The registry entry point consumes the run-lineage reference recorded on model versions — an API-level artifact produced by the Model Registry epic. |
| E001 → E004 | 11 (docs-authoring last) | Documentation describes the implemented comparison workflow; blocked by all Implementation epics. |
| E002 → E004 | 11 (docs-authoring last) | Same. |
| E003 → E004 | 11 (docs-authoring last) | Same — HLR-4 requires coverage of the registry-initiated comparison path. |
| (no edge) E001 ∥ E002 | 14 (different repos, no shared artifacts) | Dashboard (odh-dashboard) and Model Registry (model-registry) are separate repos with no shared build-against artifact at this stage — deliberately parallel. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Coverage |
|-----|----------|---------|----------|
| HLR-1 — select two or more runs, view parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard | P0 | E001 | Full (side-by-side comparison view) |
| HLR-2 — registered model versions link back to the run that produced them; comparison openable from the Model Registry | P1 | E002, E003 | Full (E002: lineage metadata; E003: registry UI entry point) |
| HLR-3 — run diff view highlighting changed parameters and metrics | P1 | E001 | Full (diff mode of the comparison view; bundled per Step 4) |
| HLR-4 — documentation covers the comparison workflow from runs list and registry | P2 | E004 | Full |

No orphaned HLRs; every HLR maps to at least one epic.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no NFRs.
  Teams were inferred from the architecture context owning-team fields
  (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard; Model Registry → Model Registry). The
  documentation team ("RHOAI Documentation") is inferred — no architecture
  context file exists for the Documentation component. Human verification of
  team assignments recommended.
- **Passive component classification**: Data Science Pipelines is listed as
  affected but no HLR requires a change to it; it is treated as
  keep-working/passive with a validation AC on E001. If bulk comparison
  actually requires a pipelines-side API change, E001's scope grows — this is
  an implementation detail, not an unknown that changes the epic structure.
- **Docs priority inversion (mild)**: HLR-4 is P2 but the docs-authoring epic
  is P1 due to the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority
  Major → P1). Flagged for human review of relative scheduling.
- **Source overlap**: the strategy notes requirements were consolidated from
  two customer councils with overlapping wording kept — minor ambiguity risk
  in requirement intent.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing; all work is
in-platform.

# Decomposition Review — RHAISTRAT-9015

## Review Summary

Score: 14/14 — pass
Recommendation: accept

Reviewed against the strategy (RHAISTRAT-9015, Refinement Done, Major), the
decomposition summary, 4 epic files, and 4 AI signal rationale files. No
conditional branch files exist (none required — no open questions or external
dependencies). Architecture context verified: dashboard.md, model-registry.md,
and data-science-pipelines.md all present under rhoai-3.0; owning-team fields
(RHOAI Dashboard, Model Registry) match the epic assignments. Triage is null
(full decomposition), so the 4-epic output is expected and not penalized.

## Criterion Details

### 1. HLR Coverage (2/2)
All four HLRs map to at least one epic: HLR-1 (P0) → E001; HLR-2 (P1) → E002 +
E003 (correctly split by component); HLR-3 (P1) → E001; HLR-4 (P2) → E004.
Traceability matrix is present in the summary and mirrored in each epic's HLR
Traceability section. Priority inheritance is sound: E001 (P0) blocks only
lower-or-equal priority work (E003 P1, E004 P1); E004's P1 (vs HLR-4's P2)
correctly applies the docs-authoring exception (strategy priority Major → P1).
Minor (no score impact): E001 bundles HLR-1 (P0) with HLR-3 (P1) — the diff
view is a distinct user-facing capability, but the bundling is explicitly
justified by shared UI surface and data plumbing (same component, team, and
view; splitting would revisit the same surface), which is a defensible
Step-4 coupling call rather than priority collapse of independently
deferrable work.

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)
No cycles. Every diagram edge has a matching frontmatter dependency and vice
versa: E003 depends on [E001, E002]; E004 depends on [E001, E002, E003]; E001
and E002 are roots. Arrows are drawn dependency → dependent per convention.
Edges are justified: E001→E003 (surface → consumer, rule 13), E002→E003
(lineage artifact consumer, rule 13), and the three edges into E004 are valid
rule 11 docs-authoring edges. E001 ∥ E002 correctly preserve parallelism
(separate repos, no shared artifact). Critical path length 3 fits the
strategy size (S/M standard: 3-4). No konflux-onboarding epics exist, so
rules 7/8/10 parallelism constraints are not applicable. No branch files, so
branch/gated_by checks are not applicable. No uncaptured data dependencies:
E003's scope explicitly names its two upstream capabilities and both are DAG
edges.

### 3. Epic Boundaries (2/2)
Each epic is a single component/team tuple: E001/E003 (Dashboard, RHOAI
Dashboard), E002 (Model Registry, Model Registry), E004 (Documentation, RHOAI
Documentation). HLR-2 is correctly split along the component boundary
(metadata vs UI entry point) rather than bundled. No scope duplication: E003
adds an entry point to the comparison view E001 builds without rebuilding it;
E002 produces the lineage E003 consumes. Code implementation (E001-E003) is
cleanly separated from content authoring (E004). Each epic is plausibly
single-sprint sized.

### 4. Type Correctness (2/2)
All four epics are Implementation; each produces a concrete artifact (UI
view, lineage metadata, UI entry point, documentation). No Investigation
epics — justified: the strategy states "Open Questions: None" and the summary
explains why remaining unknowns (bulk-fetch mechanics, lineage storage) are
implementation details that do not change epic structure. No gated_by or
gate_failure_impact fields are set anywhere, and none are needed (no
Investigation dependencies). E004 correctly carries
implementation_type: docs-authoring.

### 5. AI Implementability Scoring (2/2)
All epics are Implementation type and carry ai_signals (the 9-signal rubric);
no epic mixes in investigation_signals. Signal values are consistent with the
strategy content: e.g., E001/E003 external_dependency 1 (all work in the
Dashboard repo) vs E002 external_dependency 0 (model-registry is
upstream-derived, contribution possible — neutral), E004 human_process_gates
-1 (docs content process plus mandatory technical review), E004 repo_access 0
(docs tooling access unconfirmed). Rationale files exist for all four epics
and match the frontmatter values. Minor (no score impact): the
human_process_gates asymmetry between E001 (0, hedged on possible undeclared
UX review for a new UI surface) and E002 (1, "no human approval steps
declared") is arguable, but each rationale supports its own value and the
difference is defensible (new user-facing surface vs metadata-only change).

### 6. Acceptance Criteria Quality (2/2)
Every epic has testable acceptance criteria derived from the strategy. E001's
ACs cover multi-select side-by-side rendering, the diff view, passive
validation against Data Science Pipelines runs, and enforcement of the
strategy's out-of-scope boundary (no cross-project/cross-cluster comparison).
E002 includes a backward-compatibility AC for pre-existing model versions.
E003 covers both the happy path and graceful handling of versions without
lineage. E004 (docs-authoring) includes the rule-mandated technical-review
AC. No replacement epics (no rollback/feature-flag AC required) and no
konflux-chain epics (no build pipeline AC required). No epic body references
sibling epics by draft ID — E003 refers to "other work in this strategy"
without naming E001/E002.

### 7. Completeness (2/2)
The combined epic set covers the full strategy scope: runs-list multi-select
and side-by-side view (E001), diff view (E001), run lineage on model versions
(E002), registry-initiated comparison (E003), and documentation of both entry
paths (E004). The strategy's out-of-scope items are explicitly carried into
E001's scope. Data Science Pipelines is handled as a passive component with
an explicit validation AC on E001 — no HLR requires a pipelines change, and
the summary flags the residual risk if a pipelines-side API change turns out
to be needed. Strategy-level context is carried forward: the
spreadheets-to-platform problem statement appears in E001's description, the
two-council source overlap is recorded in the summary's health warnings, and
team-inference caveats are documented. Documentation support is required
(HLR-4) and E004 exists, satisfying Rule 11.
